summary_paragraph: James, a man with a history of heavy alcohol use, COPD, and chronic pain from prior injuries, was admitted after being found unresponsive on a sofa. He presented with pneumonia, alcohol and benzodiazepine intoxication, and hypoxia. He received initial treatment with levofloxacin and flagyl in the ED, but due to prior resistance, was switched to Bactrim. He refused further testing, including a CT for possible pulmonary embolism, and declined breathing treatments, nicotine replacement, and social work support. He was treated for alcohol withdrawal with diazepam and showed some improvement in oxygen levels. Despite medical advice, he chose to leave the hospital against medical advice on the second day of admission, after receiving only two days of appropriate antibiotic therapy.
problems: Acute alcoholic intoxication in alcoholism, continuous
